tasks.description: Create a `Student` dataclass with `name: str`, `grades: list = field(default_factory=list)`. Add an `average()` method.
tasks.hint:
`from dataclasses import dataclass, field`
`@dataclass class Student: name: str; grades: list = field(default_factory=list)`
`def average(self): return sum(self.grades) / len(self.grades) if self.grades else 0`
tasks.solution:
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

@dataclass
class Student:
    name: str
    grades: list = field(default_factory=list)

    def average(self):
        return sum(self.grades) / len(self.grades) if self.grades else 0

alice = Student('Alice', [90, 85, 92])
bob = Student('Bob')
print(alice)
print(alice.average())
print(bob.average())
tasks.walkthrough:
The dataclass gives you the constructor and a readable print for free.
`average` uses a conditional expression so a student with no grades returns 0 instead of dividing by zero.

tasks.description: Create a `GradeBook` class that holds a list of Students. Add `add_student()`, `get_student(name)`, and `class_average()` methods.
tasks.hint:
`self.students = []` in `__init__`.
`get_student`: loop and return matching student, or `None` if not found.
`class_average`: `sum(s.average() for s in self.students) / len(self.students)`
tasks.walkthrough:
`get_student` loops until it finds a matching name and returns None if it never does.
`class_average` averages each student's average, with an empty-book guard.

tasks.description: Add a method `top_student()` that returns the student with the highest average grade.
tasks.hint:
`max(self.students, key=lambda s: s.average())` returns the student with the highest average.
Handle empty list case: `if not self.students: return None`
tasks.walkthrough:
`max` with a key function compares students by their average and returns the one with the highest.
The empty-list check avoids the ValueError that `max` raises on nothing.

tasks.description: Add `save_to_csv(filename)` and `load_from_csv(filename)` class methods to persist the grade book.
tasks.hint:
Save: write each student's name + grades as CSV rows.
Load: read CSV, reconstruct Student objects.
Use `csv.writer` for saving, `csv.reader` for loading.
tasks.walkthrough:
Each student becomes one CSV row: the name followed by all the grades, however many there are.
`load_from_csv` is a classmethod that builds a fresh GradeBook, reads each row, and reconstructs a Student with the grades converted back to floats.

tasks.description: Create a simple CLI menu: 1) Add student, 2) Add grade, 3) View report, 4) Save & Exit. Loop until exit.
tasks.hint:
`while True: choice = input('1/2/3/4: ')` with if/elif branches.
For 'Add grade': get student name first, then `student.grades.append(float(grade))`.
'View report': loop students, print name and average.
tasks.walkthrough:
The loop shows the menu, reads a choice, and branches. Each branch does one small job using the GradeBook methods.
Option 4 saves and then `break`s out of the loop. The `else` handles typos without crashing.

lesson.intro:
A project that pulls together dataclasses, classes, CSV files and a menu loop.
A student has grades; a grade book holds students and can report on them. Build
it up one task at a time and run after each. The solutions show one reasonable
design, not the only one.

sections.heading: The data: a Student dataclass
sections.body:
A name and a list of grades. `default_factory=list` so every student gets
a fresh list. A method for the average, guarded against an empty list.

sections.heading: The container: a GradeBook class
sections.body:
Holds a list of students and knows how to find one by name and compute
the overall average. `max` with a `key` finds the top student.
sections.output: (see the solutions for a full version)

sections.heading: Saving and loading
sections.body:
One CSV row per student: the name, then the grades. Loading reads each row
back, converts the grades to floats, and rebuilds the objects. A
`@classmethod` is a natural home for "make a GradeBook from a file".

sections.heading: The menu loop
sections.body:
Print the options, read a choice, branch with if/elif, repeat until exit.
Keep each branch short by calling methods on the grade book rather than
doing the work inline.

watch_out: Dividing by `len(self.grades)` when it's zero. Guard it.
Reading grades back from CSV as strings and then averaging them. Convert to float.
Letting the menu crash on an unknown choice. An `else: print('Unknown option')` keeps it polite.
In this app, put every menu answer on its own line in the input box, ending with the exit option.
